answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when every identity must plant a stake before it can graze: joining requires locking a refundable bond that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. A ridge of independent verifiers, randomly sampled peers who re-check a newcomer's past work, raises the cost further, since each fake must pass fresh scrutiny instead of cloning one reputation. The quartz-hard proof comes from tying the bond to a single hardware-backed key, so one operator cannot mint a thousand selves for free. Fakes become expensive; honest agents keep their stake.
